canDo.en: I can express a cautious, well-qualified position in academic writing, using hedging, impersonal structures and nominalisation, and I can recognise how strongly a writer commits to a claim.
canDo.bg: Мога да изразя внимателна, добре обоснована позиция в академичен текст чрез смекчаване, безлични конструкции и номинализация и мога да разпозная доколко авторът се ангажира с едно твърдение.

title.en: Hedging: claiming as much as the evidence allows
title.bg: Смекчаване: твърдиш толкова, колкото позволяват доказателствата

body.en: Academic English rarely states things as absolute fact. Writers signal how certain they are with modal verbs (may, might, could), lexical verbs (appear, seem, suggest, indicate), adverbs (arguably, possibly, largely, to some extent) and impersonal frames (It would appear that…, It could be argued that…, There is some evidence that…). "The data prove that…" is a much stronger claim than "The data suggest that…", and examiners and reviewers notice the difference. Bulgarian academic prose also hedges, but uses it less densely, and Bulgarian writers often translate "доказва" as "proves" where English would expect "shows" or "suggests".
body.bg: Академичният английски рядко представя нещо като абсолютен факт. Авторите показват степента си на увереност чрез модални глаголи (may, might, could), смислови глаголи (appear, seem, suggest, indicate), наречия (arguably, possibly, largely, to some extent) и безлични конструкции (It would appear that…, It could be argued that…, There is some evidence that…). "The data prove that…" е много по-силно твърдение от "The data suggest that…" и рецензентите забелязват разликата. Българският академичен стил също смекчава, но по-рядко, а българските автори често превеждат "доказва" като "proves", където на английски се очаква "shows" или "suggests".

examples: It would appear that the policy has had little effect.
The results suggest a link between sleep and memory.
This is arguably the most important factor.
To some extent, the problem is one of funding.

body.en: Academic writing often packs a whole clause into a noun phrase: "Because prices rose sharply, demand fell" becomes "The sharp rise in prices led to a fall in demand". Nominalisation lets you make the process (not the people) the subject, compress information, and build cautious claims around abstract nouns ("The reduction in interaction may…"). Note the knock-on changes: adverbs become adjectives (rose sharply → sharp rise) and verbs need prepositions (reduce interaction → a reduction in interaction). Bulgarian bureaucratic style also overuses nouns ("извършване на проверка"), so aim for clarity: nominalise where it helps the argument, not everywhere.
body.bg: Академичното писане често свива цяло изречение в именна фраза: "Because prices rose sharply, demand fell" става "The sharp rise in prices led to a fall in demand". Номинализацията позволява процесът (а не хората) да е подлог, сгъстява информацията и дава основа за предпазливи твърдения около абстрактни съществителни ("The reduction in interaction may…"). Обърни внимание на промените: наречията стават прилагателни (rose sharply → sharp rise), а глаголите изискват предлози (reduce interaction → a reduction in interaction). Българският канцеларски стил също злоупотребява със съществителни ("извършване на проверка"), така че целта е яснота: номинализирай там, където помага на аргумента, а не навсякъде.

texts.title: Remote work and productivity: a discussion
paragraphs: The rapid expansion of remote work since 2020 has prompted considerable debate about its effect on productivity. Early studies reported substantial gains; however, these findings would appear to rest largely on self-reported data, which are notoriously vulnerable to bias.

More recent research presents a less uniform picture. While employees performing routine, individual tasks seem to benefit from the absence of office distractions, the evidence suggests that collaborative and creative work may suffer when face-to-face contact is limited. The reduction in informal interaction is arguably the most significant cost, since it is difficult to measure and its consequences may only become visible over time.

Methodological differences complicate matters further. Studies vary widely in how they define productivity, ranging from output per hour to managers' subjective ratings, which makes direct comparison problematic.

It should be noted that much of the existing literature focuses on large technology firms, whose experience cannot necessarily be generalised to smaller organisations or to the public sector. To some extent, therefore, the question of whether remote work increases productivity remains open. A more productive line of inquiry might be to ask which tasks, under which conditions, are best performed remotely.

objective.en: Choose an appropriately cautious reporting verb.
objective.bg: Да избереш подходящо предпазлив глагол за докладване.

items.prompt: A single survey of 200 students found that those who slept more had higher grades. Which sentence best reports this finding in an academic essay?
options: The survey proves that sleep causes better grades.
The survey shows clearly that sleep is the reason for good grades.
The survey suggests that there may be a link between sleep and academic performance.
It is a fact that students who sleep more get higher grades.

explanation.en: One survey can show a correlation but cannot prove causation. "Suggests… may be a link" matches the strength of the evidence. The other options overclaim: "proves", "shows clearly that sleep is the reason", and "it is a fact" all present a correlation as a proven cause.
explanation.bg: Едно проучване може да покаже връзка, но не и причинно-следствена зависимост. "Suggests… may be a link" отговаря на силата на доказателствата. Другите варианти преувеличават: "proves", "shows clearly that sleep is the reason" и "it is a fact" представят корелацията като доказана причина.

hints.en: Can one survey prove that one thing causes another?
hints.bg: Може ли едно проучване да докаже, че едно нещо причинява друго?

items.sentence: It would ___ that the new policy has had little measurable impact on attendance.

explanation.en: "It would appear that…" (or "It would seem that…") presents a conclusion tentatively: this is how it looks on the evidence, but the writer stops short of full commitment. "Would" adds an extra layer of caution compared with "It appears that…".
explanation.bg: "It would appear that…" (или "It would seem that…") представя извода предпазливо: така изглежда според данните, но авторът не се ангажира напълно. "Would" добавя още една степен на предпазливост в сравнение с "It appears that…".

objective.en: Rewrite a clause as a noun phrase.
objective.bg: Да преобразуваш изречение в именна фраза.

accept: The sharp rise in unemployment led to social unrest.
Social unrest led to the sharp rise in unemployment.

explanation.en: This nominalises "Unemployment rose sharply, which led to social unrest". The verb "rise" becomes the noun "rise", the adverb "sharply" becomes the adjective "sharp", and "in" links the noun to what rose.
explanation.bg: Това е номинализация на "Unemployment rose sharply, which led to social unrest". Глаголът "rise" става съществително "rise", наречието "sharply" става прилагателно "sharp", а "in" свързва съществителното с това, което е нараснало.

hints.en: The subject is a noun phrase: The sharp rise in…
hints.bg: Подлогът е именна фраза: The sharp rise in…

objective.en: Use the right preposition after a nominalised verb.
objective.bg: Да използваш правилния предлог след номинализиран глагол.

items.sentence: The study found a significant reduction ___ waiting times after the reform.

explanation.en: When "reduce" becomes a noun, the thing reduced follows "in": a reduction in costs, an increase in demand, a rise in prices. "Of" is a common error, partly because Bulgarian uses "на" (намаляване на времето).
explanation.bg: Когато "reduce" стане съществително, намаленото нещо следва след "in": a reduction in costs, an increase in demand, a rise in prices. "Of" е честа грешка, отчасти защото на български казваме "намаляване на времето".

hints.en: Same preposition as in "an increase ___ prices".
hints.bg: Същият предлог като в "an increase ___ prices".

items.prompt: "This is arguably the most important novel of the decade." What does "arguably" signal?
options: The claim is controversial and probably wrong.
People are arguing about the novel.
The writer is quoting someone else's opinion.
The writer believes the claim and thinks it can be reasonably defended.

explanation.en: "Arguably" means "it can be argued that" — the writer puts forward the claim as their position, while acknowledging others might disagree. It does not mean the claim is doubtful or that people are literally arguing.
explanation.bg: "Arguably" значи "може да се твърди, че" — авторът представя твърдението като своя позиция, но признава, че други може да не са съгласни. Не значи, че твърдението е съмнително или че хората буквално спорят.

hints.en: It comes from "it can be argued", not "an argument" between people.
hints.bg: Идва от "it can be argued" (може да се твърди), а не от спор между хора.

objective.en: Choose a hedge that limits a claim's scope.
objective.bg: Да избереш смекчаване, което ограничава обхвата на твърдение.

items.prompt: Which sentence makes the most carefully limited claim?
options: Social media has completely changed how young people read.
To some extent, social media appears to have changed how some young people read.
Social media has certainly changed how young people read.
Undoubtedly, social media changes how everyone reads.

explanation.en: "To some extent" limits the degree, "appears to" softens the certainty, and "some young people" limits the scope. The other options use boosters (completely, certainly, undoubtedly, everyone) that commit the writer to a claim that is hard to defend.
explanation.bg: "To some extent" ограничава степента, "appears to" смекчава увереността, а "some young people" ограничава обхвата. Другите варианти използват усилватели (completely, certainly, undoubtedly, everyone), които ангажират автора с трудно защитимо твърдение.

hints.en: Count the hedges in each option.
hints.bg: Преброй смекчаващите елементи във всеки вариант.

accept: It could be argued that the reform came too late.

explanation.en: "It could be argued that…" introduces a position without saying "I think". The impersonal passive keeps the focus on the argument and allows the writer to evaluate it later.
explanation.bg: "It could be argued that…" въвежда позиция, без да казваш "I think". Безличната страдателна конструкция задържа фокуса върху аргумента и позволява на автора да го оцени по-късно.

objective.en: Identify why a writer questions earlier research.
objective.bg: Да откриеш защо авторът поставя под въпрос по-ранни изследвания.

items.prompt: Why does the writer treat the early studies with caution?
options: They were carried out before 2020.
They only studied creative workers.
They mainly relied on what workers said about themselves, which can be biased.
They found that remote work reduced productivity.

explanation.en: The writer says the findings "would appear to rest largely on self-reported data, which are notoriously vulnerable to bias". Note that even this criticism is hedged ("would appear to", "largely").
explanation.bg: Авторът казва, че резултатите "would appear to rest largely on self-reported data, which are notoriously vulnerable to bias". Забележи, че дори тази критика е смекчена ("would appear to", "largely").

hints.en: Look at the end of the first paragraph.

objective.bg: Да определиш цялостната позиция на автора.

items.prompt: Which statement best reflects the writer's overall position?
options: The effect of remote work probably depends on the type of task, and the evidence is not yet conclusive.
Remote work clearly harms productivity and should be limited.
Remote work clearly increases productivity for most organisations.
There is no useful research on remote work.

explanation.en: The writer says the question "remains open" "to some extent" and proposes asking "which tasks, under which conditions, are best performed remotely". The text balances benefits for routine tasks against costs for collaborative work — it argues neither for nor against remote work overall.
explanation.bg: Авторът казва, че въпросът "remains open" "to some extent" и предлага да се пита "which tasks, under which conditions, are best performed remotely". Текстът балансира ползите за рутинни задачи и загубите при съвместна работа — не е нито за, нито против дистанционната работа като цяло.

objective.en: Identify a limitation noted by the writer.
objective.bg: Да откриеш ограничение, посочено от автора.

items.sentence: According to the writer, much of the existing research has focused on large ___ firms.

explanation.en: The third paragraph says: "much of the existing literature focuses on large technology firms", which may not represent smaller organisations or the public sector.
explanation.bg: Третият абзац казва: "much of the existing literature focuses on large technology firms", които може да не са показателни за по-малки организации или за публичния сектор.

hints.en: Read the first sentence of the last paragraph.
hints.bg: Прочети първото изречение на последния абзац.
